- (akr) Evidence records routinely cite `.agent/scratch` paths as their `artifact`, but scratch is documented as prunable and nothing stops a cited path being deleted: 38 records across 5 .akr files reference `.agent/scratch/...`. Most are already dangling — when `.agent/scratch/ocr-benchmark` was inspected on 2026-08-22 it held only score.py, b3.*, target/ and three recipe output dirs, while eight separate evidence records cite sibling paths under it (tensorrt-smoke-*, lazy-corrected-*, out-winocr-12mp-200-sharded, release-auto-winocr-*, release-tensorrt-*, turboocr-*.txt) that had already been pruned. Those verified claims silently lost their backing. The fix belongs in `knowledge.evidence_add`: it should refuse an `artifact` path under the scratch root outright, at write time, and tell the author to move the artefact somewhere durable first. Refusing at the point of writing is what makes the guarantee hold — a warning emitted later by `akr build` or `validate` arrives after the record is already in the ledger, and by then the usual outcome is a dangling reference nobody re-reads. A durable-path precondition is cheap to check and turns an unenforced convention into an invariant.  `@lege-ecosystem.papercut.evidence-records-routinely-cite-agent-scratch/2`
